title: The Patient Well
premise: Freya Hartwell, an urban explorer who maps tunnels missing from every city survey, inherits her grandmother's house and discovers that every photograph taken inside it now contains an extra chair—and sometimes the suggestion of someone sitting in it. The tunnels beneath converge on a sealed well where the town's founders bound an unjustly condemned woman, whose patience has outlasted their bloodline. As the last living founder's heir arrives to sign away the property, Freya learns she is the unintended inheritor of both the debt and the ritual. She completes the founders' unfinished rite—not to imprison the woman again, but to release her—burning her own name from the deed so the house, and she, can finally be seen on their own terms.
about_author: Ulyana Reyes is a former municipal archivist who spent years cataloguing properties with gaps in their legal histories. She writes horror about paperwork, place, and the people history decided not to count.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. After her grandmother's funeral, Freya moves into the house to sort the estate, keeping her routines: lights on, doors counted, photographs logged. She notices every image now includes a wooden chair no one owns, positioned closer each day. Exploring the cellar, she finds a hatch to unmapped tunnels. Emotional beat: unease curdling into obsession—the comfort of control beginning to fail.

chapters.title: What the Survey Missed
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, intercut with journal entries from founder Elias Marsh, 1891. Following the tunnels, she reaches a bricked well ringed with names scratched out except one: Maren Voss, hanged without trial. The chair appears in the tunnels now, waiting at junctions. A lawyer calls: an heir named Corliss wants to buy the estate quickly. Emotional beat: dread mixed with fierce curiosity—Freya starts wanting to know Maren.

chapters.title: The Last Signature
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Freya and Corliss, the founders' final descendant, who arrives desperate to sign before winter solstice. He confesses the ritual was left half-finished: the binding holds only while a founder's heir holds the deed. The well opens; Maren's presence fills the house, gentle but vast, asking not vengeance but witness. Corliss tries to flee and sell anyway. Emotional beat: terror giving way to moral clarity—Freya chooses belonging to the wronged over safety.

chapters.title: Counted Doors, Open Well
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On the solstice, Freya completes the rite in reverse: she speaks Maren's name into the record, burns the fraudulent condemnation order, and signs the deed over to no one—an inheritance refused. The extra chair empties; the photographs settle. The tunnels collapse behind her as she walks out into daylight, finally visible, finally home in a house that belongs to its own history. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into peace and hard-won justice.
